GLOBAL ATMOSPHERIC CIRCULATION CRAP 

Hadley cell and all that bollocks 

HADLEY CELL – At the equator, the sun’s rays are more concentrated, so the air is warmer. This warm air rises, bringing low pressure (rain and clouds). When the air reacts around 30 degrees north/south, the sun’s rays are sparser, causing the air to be cooler, so it sinks, bringing high pressure (clear skies and no rain).  

POLAR CELL – At the North/South poles, the sun’s rays are extremely sparse, causing the air to be very cold, making it sink – causing high pressure. When the air reaches 60-70 degrees north/south, the sun’s rays are more concentrated, causing the air to be warmer, so the air rises, bringing low pressure (funnily enough the UK is at 60-70 degrees north so that basically explains the UK’s rainy shitty weather) 

FERREL CELL – in the wise words of Mr. S. Burton, “the Ferrel cell acts like a cog between the Hadley and polar cell, so once you have explained those just say it acts like a cog between them”. 

TROPICAL STORM SHIT 

Side note – A tropical storm, hurricane, typhoon and a monsoon are all the same thing it just depends on where you’re from. 

First, there needs to be a thunderstorm over water which has a temperature of at least 27 degrees C. with low crosswinds, so the thunderstorm doesn’t get torn apart. Then, due to the Coriolis effect, the thunderstorm starts spinning, causing the eye and eye wall to form. It is now technically a tropical storm. When the tropical storm hits land, it brings heavy rainfall and storm surge. It then dissipates since it can’t get any energy from the sea. 

In terms of where they form and when and all that shit, just remember this: 

They form during late summer/early autumn (like now – August-September usually) 

They form anywhere from 5-20 degrees north/south, go west at first, then go north in the northern hemisphere and south in the southern hemisphere. 

The intensity of tropical storms is predicted to increase due to climate change heating up the oceans (fucking fabulous guys). Climate change is also going to increase the number of places tropical storms can actually develop, including the south Atlantic, which previously had very few tropical storms form there however water temperatures have surpassed the 27-degree threshold there due to climate change. 

The frequency of tropical storms is actually expected to decrease. Idfk why though. 

When it comes to monitoring tropical storms the 2 main places you need to know are the National Hurricane Center in Florida and the Typhoon Warning Center in Hawaii. They track the wind speed; path the hurricane will take and predict the damage it will cause. 

Since hurricanes can kinda go wherever the fuck they want, a cone of uncertainty has to be made to cover the whole area a hurricane can technically go, so people know if their local area is at risk or not. 

When it comes to reducing the effects of tropical storms, doing hurricane drills (like a fire drill but different – America has a lot of things they need to drills for like tornadoes earthquakes etc.) will help and children will know how to act in an emergency. HICs can also build storm shelters, which are raised in concrete to prevent them from flooding, and are made of concrete so they cannot be destroyed by the strong winds or any objects the hurricane is throwing at it. However, in LICs (like Hittesh’s homeland, Sri Lanka) this isn’t an option as they are pretty expensive. 

Also, in HICs houses in high-risk areas, *cough* Florida *cough* can be built featuring stormproof windows and tiles, so the house can remain intact through a hurricane, lowering damage and improving the area’s hurricane resistance. Again, this simply isn’t possible in LICs as they are expensive.

NATURAL FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE CLIMATE CHANGE 

Easiest shit ever.  

Theres 4 you need to know, these are called “external factors” since they occur outside the atmosphere: 

Changes to the Sun’s output – If the sun outputs more solar energy, it will affect the earths climate by making it warmer. 

(just swap “more” for “less” and “warmer” for “cooler” for the reverse) 

Changes to the Earth’s orbit – Over 100,000 years, the earth’s orbit around the sun can change from a circle to an oval shape. If the earth gets closer to the sun on the oval, the earth will get more solar energy and will affect the earth’s climate by making it warmer, but if the earth reaches the edges of the oval, furthest away from the sun, the earth will get less solar energy and will affect the earth’s climate by making it cooler. 

Changes to the earth’s axial tilt – Over 41,000 years, the earth’s axis can change by 1 degree from 23.5 degrees. If it tilts closer to the sun at 22.5 degrees, the earth will get more solar energy and will affect the earth’s climate by making it warmer, however if it tilts away from the sun at 24.5 degrees, the earth will get less solar energy and will affect the earth’s climate by making it cooler. 

Wobble (love the word wobble) – Over 23,000 years, the earth can randomly wobble closer or further from the sun. If it wobbles closer to the sun, the earth will get more solar energy and will affect the earth’s climate by making it warmer, however if it wobbles away from the sun, the earth will get less solar energy and will affect the earth’s climate by making it cooler. 

Yeah. I told you, piss easy. 

Now for the internal factors (inside the atmosphere): 

Volcanic eruptions – Sulfur and ash from eruptions can block the sun’s radiation, causing the climate to be cooler. 

Tectonic Movements – Plate tectonics move the continents, leading to changes in atmospheric circulation in different parts of the world, making some areas have a warmer climate and other areas having a cooler climate. 

The albedo effect (they be pulling these names out of their ass but yk) – Snowy areas have a cooler climate partly due to snow reflecting most light incident on it, leading to the ground and therefore the climate remaining cold as most solar radiation being reflected off it. However, grass absorbs more light than it reflects, warming the ground and making the climate warmer, keeping warm areas warm and cold areas cold. 

MAN-MADE FACTORS OF CLIMATE CHANGE Basically all the shit you hear on the news about factories and landfill heating the planet 

Landfill – Humans dump unused materials like plastic bags in landfill, which releases methane gas as it decomposes, contributing to the greenhouse effect and climate change. 

Deforestation – Humans cut down trees for materials and to make space for houses, which releases CO2 into the air and makes it so that less CO2 is absorbed from the atmosphere, contributing the greenhouse effect and therefore climate change and CO2 is a greenhouse gas. 

Factories/Industry – Humans use factories to manufacture goods like chemicals. This releases a large amount of CO2 into the atmosphere, contributing to the greenhouse effect and climate change.

NEW TOPIC – ECOSYSTEMS 

Fun and easy topic, gotta love it. Also, I’m kinda fed up with all this climate change bollocks. 

Ecosystem – A natural system made up of biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) factors. 

Biotic is basically things like animals, plants (me), and trees. 

Abiotic is things like soil, air and water. 

Right, there’s a lot of writing here and I can’t be arsed writing it all so Ima just shorten it a little (you guys aren’t thick so it should be easy to understand) 

Right producers are easy they are biotic and take in glucose and oxygen and photosynthesize (basically lore accurate me) 

Primary Consumers eat the producers, they are biotic. An example is a rabbit in a grassland. 

Decomposers are insects that eat dead animals and plants and leave the energy in the soil, e.g. an earthworm in a grassland. 

Climate is the average weather over 30 years, and it’s an important driver in an ecosystem as it determines the average rainfall and temperature. Climate is an abiotic factor. The Biotics adapt to the climate. 

EQUILIBRIUM IN AN ECOSYSTEM 

Ok so equilibrium in an ecosystem is a balance between all parts of the system (although in chemistry it is where the forward and reverse reactions are happening at exactly the same rate in a closed system) 

It fairly easy, say for example if all the deer died in a forest, it would have a knock-on consequence by lowering the number of wolves and other things that eat the deer, as they either relocate or starve. (sad but true, just how nature goes) (Metallica reference intended ofc) 

Also, it doesn’t necessarily have to be animals dying, for example a forest fire would reduce the number of trees, which has a knock-on consequence of reducing the birds who reside in the trees by forcibly relocating them elsewhere.

TROPICAL RAINFORESTS 

Very solid topic 

TRs are located just north or south of the equator, in between the tropics of cancer and Capricorn. Their climate is extremely wet and humid (hell on earth for me).  

There are high year-round temperatures, around 28 degrees, the first 3 months feature heavy rainfall While July, August and September feature low amounts of rainfall. 

Let me just dump everything you need to know rq 

Soils are nutrient poor since the optimal growing conditions mean that any nutrients that the decomposers have left in the soil is immediately taken by growing plants (me) and none remains.  

Adaptations (I just remember 3) 

Epiphytes – They grow on the side of trees and get their nutrients from the air. Pretty creative. 

Emergents – Trees that grow taller than the rest to get better access to sunlight, so they grow faster. 

Buttresses – They support tree structures and provide a faster rate of o2 and co2 diffusion with a larger surface area. 

Soil leaching is where the rain washed the nutrients off the soil, leaving behind latosol, a red infertile type of soil which plants struggle to grow on. (Deforestation is a big cause of this, so if there is a 6 marker about deforestation in tropical rainforests and it wants effects, mention this)

EFFECTS OF TROPICAL RAINFOREST DEFORESTATION 

- Biodiversity loss – fairly simple, if trees are cut down animals like birds lose their homes in the trees and have to relocate elsewhere, lowering the biodiversity of the area 
    

- Infertile soil – explained earlier (soil leaching and latosol and all that bollocks) 
    

- On a global scale, deforestation causes climate change as cutting trees releases co2 and stops more co2 from being absorbed. This co2 traps heat since it is a greenhouse gas and warms the planet. 
    

- Economic benefits – LICs can benefit from using the wood (not that wood) from trees in house building, and selling the wood which gives them income, so they can invest that into healthcare and education, benefiting the whole country. STRATEGIES TO REDUCE DEFORESTATION 

Theres 4 of them, they take 5 mins each to explain, and if you think I’m doing that you can fuck right off. I’ll do 2 and we’ll call it even. 

SELECTIVE LOGGING AND REPLANTING 

Basically, loggers remove only the most valuable trees from a certain area and eventually replant the deforested area as secondary forest, which initially has a lower biodiversity than the surrounding area. Advantages include less valuable trees not being damaged, which act as habitats for animals and increase biodiversity in the area, along with the deforested area eventually being replanted, which also provides habitats for animals and stops soil from being made infertile (latosol shit again). Disadvantages include more valuable trees being deforested for a short while, which can briefly destroy animal habitats. Also, the secondary replanted forest has a lower biodiversity at first, lowering the number of species in the area. 

DEBT REDUCTION 

Countries are encouraged to conserve rainforests in exchange for a reduction for their national debt. It alleviates poverty and helps protect forests. An example is the US government agreeing to reduce Peru’s debt if they protect their rainforests. Advantages include a country having less debt, so money can be spent in areas like healthcare and education, which improves people’s quality of life and can help bring people out of poverty. Can also help build international relationships (like with the US and Peru). However, this money doesn’t mean fuck all to rich countries, since they already have enough money so have no debt to have reduced, so they will just deforest anyway. Similarly, some countries will make more money deforesting than in debt reduction, for example if someone offered you 20 quid a week to stop cutting down trees in your local forest (this example is so fucking scuffed but yk) but you make 50 quid a week doing it, why the fuck would you say yes.

PLANT ADAPTATIONS IN HOT DESERTS

Plants in hot deserts can remain dormant for up to 10 years before germinating after rain.

Located anywhere from 15-30 degrees north/south 

Continents they are on include Africa, Asia and North America, and Specific countries include The United States, India (more on that later) and Australia. 

They do not always have plants as there is virtually no precipitation and plants need very special adaptations to survive in the desert environment. The soil is also extremely infertile (here we go again), making it even harder for plants to grow.

DESERTIFICATION 

Desertification is the process by which fertile land becomes desert, usually on the fringes of existing hot deserts. It becomes drier and less productive. 

(the way I like to think about it is if you get sat next to some naughty kid in maths or smth he distracts you and you become less productive, and then you make the kid sitting next to you less productive, etc.) 

CAUSES 

- Deforestation (I’m getting SEVERE ptsd) if trees get cut down, the root system holding the soil together dies, causing the soil to become less strong, making it infertile and therefore making it easier to be desertified. 
    

- Over-cultivation - where a farmer farms his land a bit too much, which stops soil from regrowing properly and eventually leads to it becoming infertile, leading to desertification. 
    

- Population growth kind of ties in will all of this, as more people mean more food needed, so more over-cultivation, along with more deforestation, leading to more desertification. 
    

STRATEGIES TO REDUCE IT 

- Planting trees reduces desertification by holding soil together through the roots and keeping the soil strong, making it less likely to be desertified.

RIVER LANDSCAPES 

My personal favorite geography topic of all time 

Source – The start of a river 

Drainage Basin – an area of land drained by a river and its tributaries 

Tributary – a small stream that joins a large river 

Confluence – where one river joins another 

Mouth – Something Alfie uses too mu- I mean where the river meets the sea 

Watershed – the line that separates one drainage basin from another 

 RIVER CROSS PROFILES 

In the upper course, the river flows in a V shape. This is because there is not much water that is drained into the river, so there is less energy in the river, so the river cannot erode laterally (left/right) only vertically (down), causing it to form a V shape. 

In the middle course the sides of the river start to erode, as the drainage basin area is larger, meaning more water drains into there river here, so the river has more energy. This makes it possible for the river to erode both laterally and vertically, so it starts to erode the sides. 

In the lower course of the river, the sides have completely eroded. This is because the drainage basin area is now very large, so the river has a lot of water and therefore energy, so it can erode vertically and laterally a lot, causing both sides to erode and also making the river very deep.

BRADSHAW MODEL 

Right listen here. I’m tired and this is not as complicated as it seems. 

 ![](data:image/png;base64,) 

That is the Bradshaw model. Basically, it shows how different river characteristics change as you go downstream. Discharge is how much water passes a point in a second (I know what you’re thinking it’s NOT THAT (well not in this context anyway)). Everything else is self-explanatory, except for like load quantity which is just the total mass of all the things that the river is carrying, and ig load particle size, which is the average size of something the river is carrying. Slope angle is the steepness of the sides of the river. 

Rather than me explaining why all these things change just remember this structure and you should be good: 

As you go down a river, a few things happen: 

- The amount of water that gets drained into the river increases (drainage basin size increases) 
    

- This gives the river more energy 
    

- So, it can erode more (sides of the river) 
    

- AND it can carry heavier objects 
    

- Those heavy objects hit each other to become smaller 
    

- It also causes the water to move faster 
    

Just use that and you should be good 

RIVER EROSION 

Erosion sounds boring but it’s easy marks so why are you complaining 

Attrition – Where rocks hit each other or roll over each other and go from large, jagged and rough to small, rounded and smooth. 

Abrasion – Where rocks scrape the riverbanks and bed and erode it 

Hydraulic power – The force of the river water on the riverbanks and bed 

Solution (pretty cool this one) – where the river water can dissolve rocks in a chemical reaction, most commonly limestone, so the river can flow underground. 

TRANSPORTATION IN RIVERS 

Not transportation as in (redacted antisemitic comment), but instead the much more legal and fun way that rivers transport rocks. 

Traction – Upper course – Large, Jagged and rough rocks roll in a circular motion in the direction of the current. They roll since the river has very little water and therefore very little energy to carry or the rocks, making them slowly roll instead. 

Saltation (my personal favorite) – Middle Course – Smaller, more rounded but still large rocks are briefly kept up by the river, before falling back down to the riverbed, then bouncing back up again and being suspended for a few seconds, before falling again. This happens as the river has more water and therefore more energy than in the upper course, also the rocks are smaller and therefore easier to carry since they have been eroded, however the river does not have enough energy to fully keep the rocks afloat, so they  fall after a few seconds. 

Suspension – Lower Course – Very small and fine sediment is carried in the river and doesn’t fall. This happens because the lower course has the most water and therefore the most energy, and the material has been eroded fully now, so it is very light and easy to carry by the river. 

Solution – Dissolved rocks flow in the direction of the current. Happened in all 3 courses since they are very light and the river has enough energy to keep them afloat.

RIVER LANDFORMS CREATED BY EROSION 

Deposition – where the river drops materials being carried 

Larger sediment is deposited first since it is heavier and needs more energy to be carried, so it is deposited before the more fine sediment. 

WATERFALLS – Waterfalls are formed when there is hard (Alfie when he sees Bobette) rock over soft rock. The water flows over the hard rock and then over the soft rock, which then erodes through hydraulic power and abrasion. Eventually, the soft rock erodes around the hard rock, forming an overhang of the hard rock. This overhang eventually gets undercut enough so it collapses, which causes the rocks from the collapsed overhang to erode the soft rock under it (abrasion) and the force of the falling water (hydraulic power) also erodes it. This creates a plunge pool. The soft rock keeps getting eroded under the hard rock, causing more overhangs and the cycle repeats as the river retreats (mis hairline) backwards. A steep sided gorge forms where the river dips (waterfall) 

Happens in the upper course. Also, you need to know a waterfall example, the one we were taught is called High Force Waterfall (refer to this in an exam if asked), but I personally think this one looks better:

RIVER LANDFORMS CREATED BY EROSION AND DEPOSITION 

MEANDERS – Now it doesn’t actually say in my book how these guys form but I remember watching a video about it so enjoy my scuffed explanation: 

One way a meander can form is if an animal like a fox burrows near a river channel (idfk why he would but you know that’s what the video said). The soil where that burrow is is weaker than the surrounding soil, so the river (hydraulic power) erodes it faster, causing it to collapse (fox becomes homeless). The river now flows slightly towards the old burrow, and since the water is travelling fastest on the side closer to the burrow (this will be explained later), the side closer to the old burrow erodes faster and causes the river to begin to bend. The other side of the river begins to deposit sediment as the river water is traveling slower here since it has less energy, so it deposits sediment and forms a slip-off slope, which eventually forms new land. 

Copilot says it’s good so we should be alright. Also I doubt we will get asked this anyway 

The river is deepest on the outside of the meander since the water is traveling faster, so it has more energy, so it can erode vertically faster, making it deeper. 

The water on the outside of the meander flows the fastest since it experiences the least friction from the riverbed and the air, since it is the furthest from the bed or the air, making it flow faster. 

The eroded material is deposited on the inside of the meander since the water is traveling slowest (closer to channel bed and air) so it has less energy, so the river cannot carry the materials and instead deposits them, forming a slip-off slope, which eventually forms new land. 

OXBOW LAKES -   The river meanders, and on the outside of the river there is erosion, and on the inside of the river there is deposition (just explain it like normal speed energy shit). This causes the river neck to become thinner. Deposition and erosion continue, until the river neck is now very thin and both channels are very close to each other. During a flood event, the river can burst through the neck and flow in a straight line through to the other side. Some water still flows through the old meander. Deposition occurs at the start and end of the old meander, (energy deposition yk the drill) So eventually the old meander is completely cut off from the river, forming an Oxbow lake.

RIVER LANDFORMS CREATED BY DEPOSITION 

Back at this again, who would have thought it. 

FLOODPLAINS – The river flows normally. When the river floods, it bursts (mis alf) it’s banks and floods the surround area, causing it to lose speed which causes it to lose energy, making it deposit sediment in the flooded area. Heavier, larger sediment is deposited first, next to the river, as it requires more energy to carry, while smaller, more fine sediment is deposited furthest from the river as it requires the least amount of energy to carry. After the flood, the river returns to normal flow, and the deposited sediment remains in the originally flooded area, causing a raised, fertile floodplain to form.

COASTAL LANDSCAPES 

The OG geo topic, gotta love this one 

LONGSHORE DRIFT (LSD – NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH THE DRUG) – The ocean’s (I wrote river at first off instinct lmao) swash follows the direction of the prevailing wind, depositing sediment in the direction of thew wind. The backwash follows gravity, causing the sediment to be deposited straight backwards into the sea. The cycle repeats, as the next swash moves the sediment slightly in the direction of the wind again, until the sediment has been transported across the beach.

CONSTRUCTIVE WAVES  

- Break infrequently (>10 a minute) 
    

- Responsible for deposition 
    

- Long in relation to their height (redacted fatphobic comment) 
    

- Swash is more powerful than backwash 
    

- Create gently sloping beaches 
    

DESTRUCTIVE WAVES 

- Responsible for erosion 
    

- Break frequently (10-25 a minute) 
    

- Backwash is more powerful than swash 
    

- Create steep beaches 
    

- High in relation to their length 
    

SPITS AND BARS 

Spits form when longshore drift deposits sediment offshore when there is a change in the shape of the coastline. This sediment keeps getting deposited outward, forming a spit. A recurved end can form if the wind direction changes, and a sheltered salt marsh can form behind the spit. A river estuary prevents the spit from reaching land as it washes away any sediment that is deposited. 

A bar is literally the same fucking thing except there’s no river, so the spit reaches the land 

WAVE-CUT PLATFORM 

Between high tide and low tide is the high energy zone in the ocean. This high energy zone causes erosion into cliff faces through hydraulic power and abrasion, causing a wave-cut notch to form. Eventually, the wave-cut notch gets very deep into the cliff, causing the overhang to collapse, which forms a wave-cut platform. The process repeats as the cliff retreats backwards. 

Freeze thaw – Water collects in a crack (I know what you’re thinking NO ITS NOT THAT), and if the temperature goes below 0 degrees, the water freezes and expands, widening the crack (Jesus Christ this explanation is fried). The process repeats as water recollects and freezes. 

MASS MOVEMENTS 

To quote Mr. Burton directly, “This doesn’t come up on exams all that much but it’s worth knowing in case it does” 

Landslides – Where a large amount on unconsolidated material falls down a slope, usually after rainfall. 

Slumping – Where a section of a cliff falls on a line of weakness 

Rockfall – Materials on a cliff face fall and land on the bottom of the cliff.

HEADLANDS AND BAYS 

Reminds me of Malta. Tons of them there 

On a discordant coastline, there is differential erosion. Softer rock erodes more quickly than harder rock, forming a bay. The hard rock erodes slower than the soft rock, forming a headland between the 2 bays. 

COASTAL MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES 

Sea walls and all that bollocks 

HARD (don’t even think about it) ENGINEERING – Visible, Expensive, Work against nature 

e.g. Rip-Rap (aka rock armor), Sea walls, Groins (Jesus Christ this topic is so horny), gabions (caged rocks) 

SOFT (holy shit) ENGINEERING – Less visible, cheaper, work with natural processes. 

e.g. Managed retreat, dune regeneration, beach nourishment 

I physically can’t be bothered explaining everything but here’s the basics: 

Sea wall – Waves hit it and it doesn’t get eroded but it’s expensive (also kinda ugly imo) 

Rip-Rap – Absorbs wave energy but it’s ugly and can drive people away 

Groins – Stop longshore drift, keeping beaches with sand but are expensive and can be ugly 

Managed retreat – allowing low lying areas of beach to be flooded 

Dune regeneration- planting marram grass (that spiky long grass you get on sand dunes) on dunes, keeping them strong and acting as a natural barrier from the sea. 

Beach nourishment – physically adding sand/shingles (fucking hate shingles I’ve been cut by them sop many times) to a beach.

PLATE RULES 

Not like eating with your mouth closed or shit like that I mean different types of tectonic plates 

Continental plate – Thinker than Oceanic, never subducts, less dense than oceanic 

Oceanic plate – Thinner than continental, always subducts, denser than continental 

BOUNDARIES 

Again, I don’t mean boundaries as in don’t hit people or don’t say slurs, I mean types of tectonic boundaries 

Destructive Boundary – An oceanic and continental plate move together, the oceanic plate subducts under the continental plate and the land is destroyed in the magma. Volcanoes occur here since the heat and pressure from the subducting oceanic plate makes the magma less dense than the surrounding area, forcing it up through the earth. 

Remember – Volcanoes can only occur when land is being created or destroyed. 

Constructive - Where 2 plates are moving away from each other (Iceland is a great example of this) and the magma rises through the cap and cools, which can form volcanoes. 

![](data:image/png;base64,) 

AYYY FOUR HORSEMEN AGAIN 

Anyway 

Conservative Boundary – Where 2 plates are moving against each other. They can get stuck where massive pressure builds up and when it gets released, a massive earthquake can happen. California is a great example of this. Also there are no volcanoes here since land isn’t being created or destroyed. 

 HORSEMEN ARE DRAWING NEARERRRRRRRRRR 

Convergent boundary (e.g. Nepal) – 2 continental plates move towards each other; however, they can’t subduct so instead they fold on each other and form mountains. (No volcanoes created destroyed shit again yk the drill)

PREDICTION AND MONITORING 

Volcanoes are easy to predict with monitoring and volcanologists (peak job ngl) monitoring changes in the volcano. The area at risk is then evacuated is something bad is suspected. 

Earthquakes are unfortunately very hard to predict and happen randomly; however, buildings have shock absorbers in high-risk areas (Canada, Japan etc.). Plus, there are evacuation places like open fields in major cities for people to go to in case of an emergency.
